text.content:
A warp in local physics has turned every body in Gehenna into a geothermal furnace. Four colossal earthbergs, each like two volcanoes fused at the base and far bigger than ordinary planets, circle a dim, coal-like red sun amid swarms of burning mountain-sized rocks; activity grows fiercer nearer the star. Nothing stays level here, not even under artificial gravity, so ships tilt anywhere from ten to forty-five degrees or more and most crews simply switch gravity off. The gulfs between orbits are a dark minefield of hot stone and ice that blocks sight between bergs.

Chamada, innermost and deadliest, is heated by both sun and eruptions, with roughly half its surface molten at any moment. Khalas is the mildest, though its ground still scorches bare feet; it has real water, carving deep canyons. Mungoth mixes fire and ash-blackened glaciers, always either scorching or freezing. Soltheim, the farthest, is a lifeless, dark ball of ice whose volcanoes died long ago.

Oddly, Gehenna's chief residents are @UUID[Compendium.dtd40k.races.Item.dtdRaceDarkEldar]{Dark Eldarin}. Like their @UUID[Compendium.dtd40k.races.Item.dtdRaceEldarin00]{Eldarin} cousins they need a world in a gravity well for some purposes, Commorragh's place in the warp makes it unsuitable for many tasks, and the sphere's isolation suits them. Native life consists of fungi and giant insects, some of them highly aggressive; nearly everything here is out to kill someone.

Vivec, the biggest @UUID[Compendium.dtd40k.races.Item.dtdRaceDarkEldar]{Dark Eldarin} settlement, is a cluster of small arcologies above raging rivers, linked by bridges whose edges are made slick and razor-sharp for sport. Mandrakes patrol it and kill on whim, and a great temple to @UUID[Compendium.dtd40k.deities.Item.dtdDb4b4672a0d21]{Lolth} looms over the city, said to house a half-Eldarin, half-daemon servant who relays her commands. Rura Penthe is a wall-less @UUID[Compendium.dtd40k.races.Item.dtdRaceHuman0000]{Human} Imperium prison on Soltheim where cold and hunger stop escapees; those who come back get a token beating. The Dark @UUID[Compendium.dtd40k.races.Item.dtdRaceEldarin00]{Eldarin} likely tolerate it in exchange for prisoners.

The Tower of the General houses elite mercenaries serving the enigmatic General of Gehenna; they take any paid job, switch sides for more coin and seem suspiciously well informed. Nimicri is a planetoid built wholly of centimetre-sized self-replicating machines, perhaps Syrne in origin, which form roads, buildings and blocky mock people and trade fine goods for information. Acererak's Tomb is an airless, magic-reliant crypt of sealed halls and guardians, where seekers face lethal trials that reward success with knowledge.

Story Master only: adventure seeds for this sphere.

A hidden temple on Mungoth imprisons the Daemon Hircine behind traps, mazes and lesser daemons; once a century he nearly escapes until a destined hero enters and seals him again. On Soltheim, feral @UUID[Compendium.dtd40k.exaltations.Item.dtdExalWerewolf0]{Werewolf} packs are said to hunt the inmates of Rura Penthe, and inmates whisper that the wolves are really the guards.

Chamada holds rich darksteel veins, though molten flows often ruin the ore; a working mine would make someone wealthy, but local @UUID[Compendium.dtd40k.races.Item.dtdRaceDarkEldar]{Dark Eldarin} already wiped out one human expedition. Caverns beneath Vivec lead straight into Commorragh via the webway, a prize for invaders such as the @UUID[Compendium.dtd40k.races.Item.dtdRaceEldarin00]{Eldarin}, but they are guarded by cruel deathtraps built to offer false hope of escape.
